title: Plans and Pricing | Netflix Help Center
text:
Netflix plans are billed monthly on the date you signed up. We do not offer annual, multi-month, or lifetime membership plans. 

Sign up for Netflix today and choose from several payment options. You can easily change your plan or cancel at any time.

You cannot share your Netflix account outside of your household, which is a collection of devices connected to the internet at the main residence where you watch Netflix. People who are not in your household can be added as an extra member.

| Netflix Plans | Features |
| --- | --- |
| Standard with ads | Ad-supported, all games and most movies and TV shows are available. A lock icon will appear on unavailable titles. Watch on 2 supported devices at a time Watch in 1080p (Full HD) Download on 2 supported devices at a time Note: If you have Netflix with a package or through a third-party, check with your provider to confirm if an ad-supported experience is available. |
| Standard | Unlimited ad-free movies, TV shows, and games Watch on 2 supported devices at a time Watch in 1080p (Full HD) Download on 2 supported devices at a time Option to add 1 extra member who doesn't live with you |
| Premium | Unlimited ad-free movies, TV shows, and games Watch on 4 supported devices at a time Watch in 4K (Ultra HD) + HDR Download on 6 supported devices at a time Option to add up to 2 extra members who don't live with you Netflix spatial audio |

### Pricing (US Dollar)

- Standard with ads: $8.99 / month
- Standard: $19.99 / month

- Add 1 extra member for $7.99 / month with ads or $9.99 / month without ads
- Premium: $26.99 / month

- Add up to 2 extra members for $7.99 each / month with ads or $9.99 each / month without ads

 Note: Extra members have their own account and password, but their membership is paid for by the person who invited them to share their Netflix account. Your plan determines how many extra member slots you can add.

 The Basic plan has been discontinued. You can change your plan at any time. 

Depending on where you live, you may be charged taxes in addition to your membership price.

Plan prices and extra member eligibility may vary if you have Netflix through a package or add-on.

title: Streamer Subscription Prices And Tiers – Everything To Know
text:
Netflix raised pricing for all its subscription tiers as of the end of March 2026. The new pricing bumped the fee to $8.99 a month for Netflix’s Standard with Ads tier, up $1. The standard tier now costs $2 more at $19.99 per month. Its Premium plan also went up $2 to $26.99.

...

Netflix – U.S.

...

Netflix set the tone for many of the streamers as one of the first in the game when it added streaming in 2007 as an add-on to its DVD-by-mail business. The standard plan without ads costs more than double what it did in 2011, with the company openly nudging customers toward the cheaper plan with ads by keeping those prices to less than half of the ad-free level.

 Wall Street rejoiced at the streamer’s latest price hike, its second since the beginning of 2025.

- Standard with Ads: $8.99
- Standard: $19.99
- Premium: $26.99

title: Netflix Basic Is Gone: U.S. Plans, Prices and Ad-Tier Limits
text:
Netflix’s ad-free Basic plan is discontinued in the United States. The cheapest generally available option is now Standard with ads at $8.99 per month, while Standard costs $19.99 and Premium costs $26.99, according to Netflix’s U.S. plan page checked August 18, 2026. Taxes, bundle billing and eligibility can change the amount you actually pay.

The change happened in stages rather than as one worldwide cutoff. Netflix launched its first U.S. ad-supported plan in 2022, later stopped offering ad-free Basic to new and returning customers in various markets, and told investors in July 2024 that the phaseout was beginning in the United States and France.

...

## What Netflix discontinued

Netflix discontinued ad-free Basic, not its entire low-cost tier. The former Basic plan offered one simultaneous stream without commercials. Its current low-price replacement, Standard with ads, costs less than the ad-free plans but introduces advertising, licensing-based catalog restrictions and some device limitations.

Netflix originally called the ad tier Basic with Ads. It launched in the United States on November 3, 2022, at $6.99 per month as an additional choice alongside ad-free Basic, Standard and Premium. See Netflix’s launch announcement at Netflix Starting From $6.99 a Month. The current U.S. name is Standard with ads, and the 2022 launch price is no longer current.

## When the Basic phaseout happened

1. October 13, 2022: Netflix announced its ad-supported service.
2. November 3, 2022: Basic with Ads launched in the United States at $6.99 per month.
3. July 2023: Netflix had stopped accepting new ad-free Basic sign-ups in some markets, according to contemporary reporting.
4. July 18, 2024: Netflix’s shareholder letter said it was phasing out Basic in the United Kingdom and Canada and beginning the process in the United States and France. The letter is available as a Netflix Q2 2024 shareholder letter.
5. August 18, 2026: Netflix’s U.S. Help Center listed Basic as discontinued.

Because Netflix implemented the change by market and customer group, there is no reliable single worldwide “Basic ended” date.

## Current U.S. Netflix plans and prices

The following table reflects Netflix’s U.S. Help Center listing checked August 18, 2026. Prices can change, and customers billed through a wireless carrier, cable company, app-store bundle or another partner may see different charges or plan choices. Taxes may also apply. See Netflix Plans and Pricing.

| Plan | Monthly price | Ads | Simultaneous streams | Video | Downloads | Catalog and extras |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard with ads | $8.99 | Yes | 2 | 1080p / Full HD | 2 supported devices | Some titles unavailable; no extra members |
| Standard | $19.99 | No | 2 | 1080p / Full HD | 2 supported devices | Full local catalog; 1 eligible extra-member slot |
| Premium | $26.99 | No | 4 | 4K / Ultra HD + HDR | 6 supported devices | Spatial audio; up to 2 eligible extra-member slots |

Netflix lists extra-member pricing at $7.99 per month with ads or $9.99 without ads where the feature is available. Extra-member eligibility varies by country, plan and billing arrangement.

...

Unlike the original one-stream Basic plan, Standard with ads supports two simultaneous streams and Full HD playback. Netflix also lists downloads on two supported devices.

### A smaller playable catalog

“Most” movies and shows are available, but not all. Licensing restrictions can place a lock icon beside a title in search results, Top 10 rows, a title page, My List or Continue Watching. Netflix explains the restriction at Netflix lock icon on a profile or title. An ad-free plan provides access to the full catalog available in that country.

### Ads during viewing

Commercial breaks appear while you watch. That may be acceptable for a lower bill, but it changes the experience for short episodes, children’s programming and repeat viewing.

### Device and casting limits

A small percentage of older devices cannot run Netflix’s ad-supported experience because their app or operating system cannot be updated. Netflix also says casting or mirroring from a mobile device to a television is unavailable on an ad-supported experience. To check before changing plans, open Netflix and choose Get Help → Plan Compatibility. If that option is absent, Netflix says the device cannot be used with an ad-supported plan. Details are in How to check device compatibility for an ad-supported experience.

### No extra members

Netflix does not permit extra members on ad-supported plans. Accounts are intended for people who live in the same household; Standard and Premium can support extra members in eligible countries and arrangements. Netflix’s household rules are described at Sharing your Netflix account.

...

- You want no advertising and the complete local Netflix catalog.

...

## What happens to existing Basic subscribers?

New and returning customers cannot select Basic. Existing legacy accounts may receive a notice that the plan is ending or changing, with Standard with ads or Standard presented as alternatives. Netflix has not published one universal migration outcome for every legacy account, so do not assume that every Basic customer is automatically moved to the same tier.

Your Netflix email, account page and payment history are the best evidence for your account. Customers billed through Verizon, T-Mobile, a cable company or another partner may receive instructions from that provider. Netflix says price-change notices generally arrive one month before the billing date affected by the change; partner-billed customers may receive the notice from the partner. See Why your Netflix price changed.

title: Netflix Plans: Cheapest Ad-Free Option Now Costs $19.99
text:
Netflix’s cheapest ad-free plan is no longer available in the U.S. The current lineup starts with Standard with ads at $8.99 per month. Ad-free viewing now starts at $19.99 for Standard, while Premium costs $26.99 and adds 4K HDR and greater household capacity.

...

Netflix removed the old ad-free Basic plan in stages rather than through one simultaneous worldwide change. The company first stopped offering Basic to new customers in selected markets. Existing U.S. customers were subsequently affected during 2024, according to contemporaneous reporting from that period.

The current U.S. plan table confirms the end state: Basic is discontinued. The lower-priced entry point remains, but it is now an ad-supported plan. The cheapest ad-free option has effectively moved up to Standard.

This is more than a simple name change. Standard with ads is not the old Basic plan at a lower price. It includes advertising, and Netflix says some movies and shows may be unavailable because of licensing restrictions. A locked-title icon identifies content that cannot be watched on the ad-supported plan.

title: Netflix raises subscription prices across all plans in US | Reuters
text:
March 26 (Reuters) - Netflix (NFLX.O), opens new tab has increased prices on all its plans in the U.S., as the streaming giant ​pushes into new programming formats such as ‌video podcasts and live sporting events.

The company's ad-supported tier will now cost $8.99 a month, compared with $7.99 earlier, while ​prices for its standard plan rose $2 per ​month to $19.99, according to its website.

The premium ⁠plan now costs $26.99 a month, up from $24.99 earlier. ​Netflix has also increased the price of adding ​an extra member to $7.99 for ad-supported plans and to $9.99 for ad-free plans.

Netflix, which has more than 325 million subscribers, ​had scrapped its cheapest ad-free plan, called basic, ​in 2023, leaving users with its more expensive premium and ‌standard ⁠plans, as well as the standard plan with ads.

title: Netflix Basic Plan Is Gone in the US and UK: What Changed?
text:
Netflix did eliminate its Basic ad-free plan in the United States and United Kingdom, but this is not a new August 2026 change. Netflix announced the US and UK phaseout in 2023, expanded it during 2024, and currently lists Basic as discontinued.

For US subscribers, the current direct Netflix choices are Standard with ads at $8.99 per month, Standard at $19.99, or Premium at $26.99, before applicable taxes. UK customers still have Standard with adverts, but should check the UK-localized Netflix page for the current pound price.

...

## What Netflix actually removed

The discontinued plan was Basic, Netflix’s least expensive ad-free tier. It should not be confused with Basic with Ads, the name Netflix originally used for its advertising-supported plan when it launched in the US and UK in November 2022.

Netflix later renamed that ad-supported option Standard with ads in the US and Standard with adverts in the UK. It remains available, but it is not an identical replacement for ad-free Basic: it includes commercial breaks, has some licensing-related title restrictions, and may not work on older devices.

Netflix’s current Help Center pricing page explicitly says: “The Basic plan has been discontinued.”

## When did Netflix remove Basic?

The timing is important because headlines describing Netflix as having “just” axed Basic are misleading.

- November 3, 2022: Netflix launched its ad-supported plan in the US at $6.99 per month and in the UK at £4.99 per month. Those were launch prices, not current prices.
- July 2023: Netflix announced that it was removing ad-free Basic for new and rejoining members in the US and UK.
- January 2024: Netflix said it planned to retire Basic in the UK during the second quarter as part of a broader rollout.
- October 2024: Netflix reported that it had phased out Basic in the US and France during the preceding quarter.
- August 2026: Netflix’s current plan documentation continues to list Basic as discontinued.

There was not necessarily one universal cancellation date for every subscriber. The rollout varied by market, account status, billing arrangement, and whether someone was a new, returning, or existing member.

Netflix’s initial announcement applied to new and rejoining members, while existing subscribers were initially allowed to keep Basic. Later disclosures confirmed that the US phaseout had been completed. That is why different customers may have received different notices or seen the change at different times.

## Current Netflix plans in the US

The following prices and features are those shown on Netflix’s US Help Center page as of August 18, 2026. Netflix can change prices, taxes may apply, and customers billed through a provider may see different options.

| Plan | Monthly price | Ads | Resolution | Simultaneous devices | Downloads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard with ads | $8.99 | Yes | 1080p Full HD | 2 | 2 supported devices |
| Standard | $19.99 | No | 1080p Full HD | 2 | 2 supported devices |
| Premium | $26.99 | No | 4K Ultra HD + HDR | 4 | 6 supported devices |

Netflix also lists extra-member options for some Standard and Premium customers. Availability and pricing depend on the country and billing arrangement. Extra members cannot be added to ad-supported plans.

...

Kids profiles do not have ads, although the ad-supported catalog’s licensing restrictions may still apply.

...

## The bottom line

Netflix did eliminate its cheapest ad-free Basic plan in the US and UK, but it did not newly do so in 2026. The US phaseout was reported as complete in 2024, and Netflix’s current documentation still lists Basic as discontinued.

The cheapest current direct US option is Standard with ads at $8.99 per month. The cheapest ad-free option is Standard at $19.99 per month. Standard with ads may save money, but it is not equivalent to the old Basic plan because of advertising, locked titles, device compatibility limits, casting restrictions, and the lack of extra-member support.

title: Netflix Price Hike Reflects Broader Shift Away From Ad-Free Streaming
text:
Netflix’s latest price increase, which began rolling out March 26, raises its standard ad-free plan from $17.99 to $19.99 per month. The premium tier now costs $26.99, while its ad-supported plan has increased to $8.99.

...

Netflix has already eliminated its lowest-priced ad-free tier, directing users toward either more expensive plans or ad-supported options. Amazon has taken a similar approach by introducing ads to its base Prime Video experience. Disney+ and Hulu have also expanded ad-supported tiers and adjusted pricing structures to encourage their use.

title: Netflix Raises German Prices Up to 10% as Premium Plan Hits €21.99 | Meyka
text:
Ad-supported tier rises 40% to €6.99, free base plan discontinued.

...

Netflix raised prices across Germany on September 4, 2026, marking its first increase in over two years. The premium 4K plan climbs to €21.99 from €19.99, while the ad-supported tier jumps 40% to €6.99. The company is also discontinuing its free ad-supported base plan for existing customers. Netflix justified the move by citing expanded content and new features, even as it faces tighter competition from Amazon Prime Video, which held 26% German market share versus Netflix’s 25% in Q4 2025.

...

Netflix’s premium plan with 4K quality and spatial audio now costs €21.99 monthly, up from €19.99. The standard plan without ads rises to €15.99 from €13.99. The ad-supported tier jumps to €6.99 from €4.99, a 40% increase. Extra household members pay €4.99 with ads or €5.99 without, up from €3.99 and €4.99 respectively. Existing customers receive one month’s notice via email before the price takes effect on their billing date.

## Netflix phases out its cheapest option

The ad-free base plan is being discontinued in Germany. Existing customers still on this tier must upgrade to standard or premium pricing or cancel. Netflix stated it continuously increases value to members, justifying occasional price rises. New customers cannot purchase the base plan at all. The move forces budget-conscious users to either accept ads or pay more for ad-free viewing.

...

What happens to existing customers on the free ad-supported plan?

The free base plan is being discontinued. Existing customers must upgrade to standard or premium pricing or cancel their subscription by their next billing date.

title: Netflix Discontinues Ad-Free Basic Plan: U.S. Prices and Ad Options
text:
Netflix’s ad-free Basic plan is discontinued in the U.S. Here are the current prices, plan features, catalog restrictions, device requirements, legacy-subscriber options, and advice on whether to choose Standard with ads, Standard, Premium, or cancel.

 iTechGuides Team iTechGuides · August 18, 2026 · 12 min read 

Netflix discontinues ad-free Basic plan availability in the United States, leaving Standard with ads as its cheapest listed tier. Netflix’s U.S. Help Center listed Standard with ads at $8.99 per month, Standard at $19.99, and Premium at $26.99 when checked on August 18, 2026. Existing subscribers should check their account notice before changing plans.

...

- Netflix’s ad-free Basic plan is discontinued in the United States; Standard with ads is now the cheapest generally available U.S. plan at $8.99 per month.
- Netflix’s U.S. lineup includes Standard with ads, Standard, and Premium at $8.99, $19.99, and $26.99 per month, respectively, according to Netflix’s plan page checked August 18, 2026.
- Standard with ads includes 1080p video, two simultaneous streams, and downloads on two supported devices, but some titles are unavailable because of licensing restrictions.
- Standard is the least expensive ad-free option at $19.99 per month and includes the full catalog available in the subscriber’s country, two streams, and 1080p video.
- Premium costs $26.99 per month and adds 4K/HDR, four simultaneous streams, downloads on six devices, spatial audio, and capacity for up to two eligible extra members.

## What happened to Netflix’s ad-free Basic plan?

Netflix discontinued the ad-free Basic plan in the United States as part of a phased, market-by-market change rather than one worldwide cutoff date. New and returning U.S. customers can no longer select Basic, while the current U.S. plan table lists Standard with ads, Standard, and Premium instead.

...

| --- | --- | --- |

...

The change does not mean Netflix eliminated its cheapest tier. Netflix replaced the old low-end choice with Standard with ads, which costs less than the ad-free plans but introduces commercial interruptions, possible catalog restrictions, and device limitations.

Netflix originally launched its U.S. ad-supported plan as Basic with Ads on November 3, 2022, at $6.99 per month. Netflix described Basic with Ads as an additional option alongside ad-free Basic, Standard, and Premium at launch, not as an immediate replacement for ad-free Basic. See Netflix’s 2022 announcement of Basic with Ads for the original launch details.

## When did Netflix phase out Basic?

Netflix phased out ad-free Basic in stages, and the timing depended on the country and the customer’s account status. Netflix’s July 18, 2024 shareholder letter said the company was phasing out Basic in the United Kingdom and Canada and beginning the process in the United States and France. Netflix’s current U.S. Help Center now confirms that Basic is discontinued in the United States.

| Date | What happened | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| October 13, 2022 | Netflix announced its ad-supported plan. | The ad-supported model was introduced as an additional plan choice. |
| November 3, 2022 | Basic with Ads launched in the United States at $6.99 per month. | The launch price is historical and is not the current U.S. price. |
| July 18, 2024 | Netflix told investors that it was phasing out Basic in the U.K. and Canada and beginning the process in the U.S. and France. | The change was a gradual regional phaseout, not a single global event. |
| August 18, 2026 | Netflix’s U.S. Help Center listed Basic as discontinued. | Basic is no longer a generally selectable U.S. plan. |

...

## What are Netflix’s current U.S. plans and prices?

Netflix’s current U.S. plan page listed three plans when checked on August 18, 2026: Standard with ads at $8.99 per month, Standard at $19.99 per month, and Premium at $26.99 per month. Taxes may apply, and prices or eligibility can differ when Netflix is billed through a wireless carrier, cable provider, app store, bundle, or another partner. The authoritative comparison is Netflix’s Plans and Pricing page.

| Plan | Monthly price | Ads | Simultaneous streams | Video quality | Downloads | Extra members |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard with ads | $8.99 | Yes | 2 | 1080p / Full HD | 2 supported devices | Not supported |
| Standard | $19.99 | No | 2 | 1080p / Full HD | 2 supported devices | 1 eligible extra member |
| Premium | $26.99 | No | 4 | 4K / Ultra HD + HDR | 6 supported devices | Up to 2 eligible extra members |

The prices shown above are U.S. prices, not global Netflix prices. Netflix says plan prices, currencies, features, catalog availability, and extra-member eligibility vary by country. Netflix’s moving-with-Netflix guidance is useful if an account or household changes countries.

...

Standard with ads is the cheapest generally available U.S. Netflix plan. The plan includes 1080p / Full HD playback, two simultaneous supported streams, and downloads on two supported devices according to Netflix’s current U.S. plan table.

The trade-off is that advertising appears during viewing. Standard with ads also does not support extra members, so the plan cannot be used as a cheaper way to add someone who lives outside the account household.

Standard with ads is not guaranteed to include every Netflix title. Netflix says most movies and shows are available, but licensing restrictions prevent some titles from appearing on the ad-supported plan. A locked title can appear in search results, Top 10 rows, a title page, My List, or Continue Watching. Netflix explains the lock icon and unavailable titles on ad-supported plans.

...

## Can former Basic subscribers keep their old plan?

New and returning U.S. customers cannot choose Basic, but Netflix’s public plan table does not describe every legacy-account transition in detail. Existing Basic subscribers should not assume that Netflix automatically moved every account to Standard with ads or that every subscriber received the same choice.

A legacy subscriber may receive an email or account notice explaining that the plan is ending or changing. Netflix may present Standard with ads or Standard as replacement options. A subscriber billed through Verizon, T-Mobile, a cable company, an app store, or another package provider may receive different instructions from that billing partner.

...

Yes. Netflix’s current U.S. Help Center lists the ad-free Basic plan as discontinued, and new or returning U.S. customers cannot select it. Existing legacy subscribers should follow the notice shown in their Netflix account or sent by their billing partner.

title: Netflix verteuert alle Abos und streicht werbefreien Basistarif – Quotenmeter.de
text:
Der Streamingmarktführer verlangt künftig mindestens 15,99 Euro für ein werbefreies Abonnement. Die Begründung mit hohen Programminvestitionen greift angesichts der Milliardengewinne zu kurz.

Netflix erhöht nach mehr als zwei Jahren erneut flächendeckend seine Preise in Deutschland. Besonders kräftig fällt der Aufschlag beim werbefinanzierten Standard-Abo aus: Statt 4,99 Euro werden künftig 6,99 Euro pro Monat fällig – ein Anstieg um 40 Prozent. Das werbefreie Standard-Paket verteuert sich von 13,99 auf 15,99 Euro, während das Premium-Abo mit 4K-Auflösung und 3D-Sound künftig 21,99 statt 19,99 Euro kostet. Zugleich lässt Netflix das werbefreie Basis-Abo endgültig auslaufen. Der Tarif war bereits seit 2023 nicht mehr für Neukunden erhältlich, konnte von Bestandskunden bislang aber für 9,99 Euro weitergenutzt werden. Diese müssen sich nun zwischen dem günstigeren Angebot mit Werbung und einem deutlich teureren werbefreien Tarif entscheiden. Damit steigt der Mindestpreis für werbefreies Netflix von 9,99 auf 15,99 Euro – um mehr als 60 Prozent. Auch das Account-Sharing wird teurer. Ein Zusatzmitglied außerhalb des eigenen Haushalts kostet im Werbetarif künftig 4,99 statt 3,99 Euro. Beim Standard- und Premium-Abo steigt der Aufpreis von 4,99 auf 5,99 Euro. In Österreich, wo das Werbe-Abo erst 2027 eingeführt werden soll, verteuert sich das Basis-Paket von 8,99 auf 10,99 Euro.
